answer: Each identity must complete a prescribed chain of modular squarings, with each result feeding the next; a Wesolowski proof lets others verify the work efficiently. GPUs can run separate chains, but cannot shortcut one chain through parallel arithmetic, so creating many plausible clones demands proportionally more hardware and wall-clock time. This bottleneck makes Sybil identities costly, not impossible—like a violet marker on a hollow river map, it signals a constraint, not a guarantee.
